mission.title: Hell-Broth
mission.description: Get the Apothecary the security she demands, intercept the Machines closing in on her, and recover the cheat code vial.

npc.say: That is not my problem. Arrange something, and quickly.
My code will function as required. I expect the Frenchman to honor the terms of the contract. I have no further duty to him or his wife.

phase.briefing: The Apothecary has nearly completed her work on the kill-code, operative, but the Machines, with their usual flair for timing, have located her, and are making nuisances of themselves--the philistines. Go see if you can't lend a hand.

enter.say:
I still think she's gonna kill us one of these days.
It'll be semi-accidental-like, sort of an "oops, you stepped in the way when I meant to target that Agent over there, sorry" type of thing, and her death-stroke will feed back along your signal and blow up our ship with me in it. Yeah, I think about these things. What else am I supposed to do while you're stuffing yourself with cake?
Okay... She's in there, and...bodies. Lots of bodies. I told you...

talk.say: I will not work without proper security to spare me from nuisances.

done.say: Operative, spare the woman your own presence, and find the General's holographic projection; it should be in a room nearby. He's agreed to let us re-route a platoon of commandos we'd been transporting for him.

talk.say: I can only spare these troops for a brief period, soldier, so make use of them while you can. The rest of the unit will be available as backup shortly, should they be needed.

done.say: Doesn't really sound like letting us borrow his platoon was his number-one plan, does it? Oh well, that's his worry. Get those two Elites out of there.

objective.text: Lead the Elites out of the area

phase.briefing:
I don't feel at all sorry for disrupting the General's troop distribution plans; after all, he'd hardly be able to get them anywhere nowadays without our help.
We'll get the others along just as soon as we can, {player}. You'll have to make do with those two for now. Intercept the inbound Machine forces.

enter.say: Got a bunch of the gearheads in there for you to test your commandos on.

done.say: Body counts continue to climb on all sides, operative. Move along before you find yourself joining them.

phase.briefing:
We need that kill-code completed, operative--much more than we need a platoon of the General's jar-heads. The Machines are getting far too close to the Apothecary for comfort, so we're throwing the General's precious troops to the wolves; they're nice and meaty, and should slow them down a bit.
You're wondering why I expend eloquence explaining this to you? Simple: you'll be viewing it first-hand. The Machines have closed in on the manufacturing facility where we had the remains of the cheat code we used as an ingredient for the new kill-code. The cheat code vial appears to have been misplaced. You're to get it back.

enter.say: I see dead people... Lots of 'em. Hm... Maybe a few Machs still kicking in there. Haven't picked up any whiff of a cheat code vial yet.

objective.text: Search for the cheat code vial

done.say: Ahh, nuts to this. That cheat code vial just isn't there. Wasn't the Apothecary done with it, anyway? Forget it. With the Machines closing in on her, we've got more immediate worries.
Everyone there is dead now, except you...so far.

phase.briefing:
Mm, yes... Despite the tragic sacrifice of the General's soldiers, some Machines have again reached the Apothecary. If they've interrupted her work a second time, there'll be the devil to pay.
You wouldn't mind looking in on her, would you, operative? Lovely.

enter.say:
Death, death, death... It's inevitable... Why fight it? Haha!
She's in there... I'm reading some Machine signals, too, dead and alive. Tra-la-la! What's the difference anymore?
Oh hey, you aren't still mad about me giving your stuff away to that maintenance ship pilot, are you? She hasn't even called me back...

done.say:
I think that's all of them... It's getting hard to tell. Everything looks dead to me now. You should ask her, I guess. She's the expert.
...If you won't be needing me for a bit, maybe I'll just go have a little lie-down.

talk.say:
My work on the kill-code is complete. Its potency is sufficient to nullify the target. The remaining packaging work necessary can be completed by any competent coder.
I am unimpressed by the Merovingian's security measures. I require him to transport me out of this simulation immediately, as is my right according to article 87.D of the contract that I have now fulfilled.

mission.finish:
A shame you failed to locate the cheat code vial, operative. It is so tiresome doing the paperwork necessary to dock your pay...
You're just fortunate that the Apothecary had no further need of it, else the consequences for you would have been dire indeed.
Even so, your incompetence has ended up driving off the only professional I've had the pleasure of working with recently. Regrettably, she did not see fit to apply the final touch to this little drama; killing you with a dismissive gesture as she left would have been the perfect parting flourish. Hm, but I suppose there's still time. You will be there to see her off, won't you?
